core_obligations: Assume each base change f_i is quasi-affine and deduce quasi-compactness and separatedness of f (proof lines 6226-6233).
Form the quasi-coherent sheaf of O_Y-algebras A = f_* O_X and the canonical morphism j : X -> Spec_Y(A) (proof lines 6234-6242).
Use flat base change to identify the pullback of f_* O_X with f_{i,*} O_{X'}, hence the base change of j with the canonical morphism of f_i (proof lines 6243-6250).
Conclude that each such morphism is a quasi-compact open immersion by the quasi-affineness characterisation, and descend that to j (proof lines 6250-6256).
Apply the characterisation once more to conclude that f is quasi-affine (proof lines 6257-6259).
proof_roadmap: Quasi-compactness and separatedness of f (proof lines 6226-6233).
The comparison morphism into the relative spectrum (proof lines 6234-6242).

difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that quasi-affineness of a morphism of schemes is fpqc local on the base (statement lines 6219-6223). The proof is displayed: assuming each base change f_i of f along an fpqc covering is quasi-affine, first f is shown to be quasi-compact and separated by the two corresponding descending lemmas; then the sheaf of algebras A = f_* O_X is formed, quasi-coherence being supplied by the pushforward lemma, and the canonical morphism j : X -> Spec_Y(A) is considered; flat base change identifies the pullback of f_* O_X with the pushforward along the base change, so the base change of j is the corresponding canonical morphism for f_i, which is a quasi-compact open immersion by the characterisation of quasi-affineness; descending these two properties along the covering gives that j is a quasi-compact open immersion, and the characterisation is applied once more to conclude that f is quasi-affine (proof lines 6225-6259). The level is H3: a complete two-stage argument, with the identification of the base-changed comparison morphism as the load-bearing step.
